column1: # Registry of RETRACTED phrasings — consumed by scripts/doc_gates.sh (gate 3).
# WHY: a correction ledger that says "this was propagated" is a CLAIM, not evidence.
# On 2026-08-01 the four-rule conflict theorem's retracted scope was still stated on the
# README front page, in TR-1's executive summary, in a figure alt-text, and in the
# CLAIMS_DECIDED row grading it REFUTED — invisible to three review passes precisely
# because TR-2's revision entry asserted the propagation was already done. This file
# makes the ledger self-enforcing: add a row when you retract something, and the gate
# fails if the retracted wording ever reappears.
# FORMAT (tab-separated, 3 columns):
#   <retracted fixed string>
column3: <note>

column1: # The allow column is matched as a substring of the "file:line:" prefix, so it exempts
# the document that legitimately quotes the old wording while explaining the retraction.
# ADD A ROW EVERY TIME YOU RETRACT OR RESCOPE A PUBLISHED CLAIM.
# THE CENSUS RULE (2026-09-02, prose batch B3 — backlog items 151 and 155)
# WHY IT IS HERE RATHER THAN IN A FINDING DOCUMENT. Five batches in one night each found a live
# site this registry could not have caught, for five structurally different reasons, and each
# wrote the lesson into its own row note. A lesson recorded five times in five notes is a lesson
# nobody applies at the sixth registration. This file is the one thing a batch is guaranteed to
# open when it registers a row, so the rule lives here and nowhere else. It is written as a
# checklist because that is the only form a later batch can be held to.
# THE PROPERTY THE WHOLE RULE DEFENDS: a needle matching nothing is NOT evidence the claim is
# gone. It may be evidence the needle cannot reach it. Every failure below is silent and
# reassuring — the census reports "1 -> 0", GATE 3 prints [ok], GATE 11 confirms the ledger
# entry, and the claim is still published. Every statement in that chain is true.
# ---- PART A: WHAT A CENSUS MUST GREP IN ADDITION TO THE REGISTERED WORDING -----------------
# Run all six before reporting a count. Each is a spelling in which the same claim survives.
#   A1. THE VALUE, ABBREVIATED. A retired number has spellings. Grep the full integer AND the
#       conventional short form, with and without digit-group commas, in every unit prefix the
#       corpus uses. (P76: one long-form occurrence and four short-form ones in one file, so a
#       grep for the integer EXONERATED it. Two earlier passes had been through that file.)
#   A2. THE CLAIM, RE-INFLECTED. Grep the claim's content words, not the registered sentence.
#       An adverb-plus-participle also appears as a hyphenated adjective, a noun phrase and a
#       relative clause. (P69: ten registered needles all spelled one form; the survivor was
#       the hyphenated adjective, and ZERO of the ten matched it when all were run mechanically.)
#   A3. CHARACTER VARIANTS. fold_variants() in scripts/doc_gates.sh normalises quotes, three
#       dash forms, the multiplication glyphs, >= and <=, four space widths and digit commas.
#       It deliberately does NOT fold backtick, ellipsis or the approximation glyphs — each a
#       measured decision recorded at the function. Grep the unfolded families by hand.
#   A4. THE LINE WRAP. git grep is line-based; GATE 3 flattens the file first. A claim spanning
#       a hard wrap is invisible to the grep that "cleared" it and visible to the gate, which
#       reports it as (spans-lines). Flatten before grepping, or trust the gate over your search.
#       (RP-face5c0c is such a site.)
#   A5. THE CORPUS BOUNDARY. GATE 3 sees the tracked *.md set plus reports/evidence/**. It does
#       NOT see .py, .c, .sh, .lean, .tsv or .txt. Grep those separately, ALWAYS, and expect
#       hits — the emitter is where a retracted claim reaches a reader who never opens a
#       document. (RP-40edf278: four roae.py sites. RP-20bac6b5: solve.py:1581 prints the
#       retired framing at run time, four lines below the docstring that withdraws it.)
#   A6. THE SAME CLAIM IN ANOTHER AUTHOR'S WORDS. Grep the claim's distinctive proper nouns and
#       its logical SHAPE — a boundary index near a universal negator, a named source near a
#       present-tense assertion — not its words. Needles-per-claim scales with the number of
#       people who ever wrote the claim, not with the number of files. (RP-9854018f: the same
#       universal, live in a second file, sharing NO substring with the first.)
# ---- PART B: HOW TO TELL WHEN NO SINGLE NEEDLE CAN COVER A CLAIM ---------------------------
# Any ONE of these is decisive. When one holds, register the sites separately and say in each
# note that it is one of N. Never widen a needle to force the sites into a single row.
#   B1. THE LIVE SITES' LONGEST COMMON SUBSTRING IS NOT THE CLAIM. If the shared span is a
#       neutral referent — a commit range, a constraint name, a file path — registering it is a
#       FALSE RETRACTION against wording the project still uses correctly. Measure the shared
#       span before choosing it. (Item 19: one claim, three grammars, three rows.)
#   B2. WIDENING WOULD SWALLOW A CORRECT LIVE USE. Test the wider needle FIRST with
#       allow=__none__ and read which files it hits; if any hit is correct prose, the wider
#       needle is dead. Measure, do not reason about it. (P68 measured and REJECTED a covering
#       needle on exactly this ground; RP-b2782ac4's note records a second rejection.)
#   B3. THE CLAIM IS NARRATED IN MORE THAN ONE FILE. The allow column holds ONE filename. Two
#       legitimate narrators need two rows, or one narrow needle per narrator. There is no third
#       option, and editing a faithful historical record so that a gate goes green is not one.
#       (RP-20bac6b5's note records the spelling that had to be given up for this reason.)
#   B4. WHAT WAS WITHDRAWN IS AN IMPLICATION OVER A TRUE PREMISE. The needle must carry the
#       implication. Registering the premise puts a false retraction on the permanent record
#       and, if a sweep follows the registration, drives correct statements out of the code.
#       (RP-9ef9344b: the premise is asserted correctly in two verifiers and one document.)
#   B5. THE SURVIVOR IS OUTSIDE THE CORPUS. No row can reach it. Disclose it by file and line in
#       the row note AND in the ledger entry, and say plainly that the row does not cover it. A
#       row that reads like coverage it does not provide is worse than no row at all.
# A census result is "<before> -> <after>" PLUS which of A1-A6 were actually run. A bare "0 hits"
# is not a census; it is one grep. And a needle must match at least one site at HEAD before it is
# registered: a row whose needle has never matched anything cannot be distinguished, later, from
# a row whose claim was swept — both print [ok] forever.

The current total is 2,760,021,104 = de Bruijn 134,217,728 + Gray orbit 256 + random Gray walks 10^5 + Latin row x column 1,625,702,400 + lexicographic 720 + random 64-permutations 10^9, with the four historical point-tests excluded because they are point-tests and not a family. The 2026-08-30 aggregate correction landed at documentation/SOLVE.md and documentation/GUIDE.md and reached three siblings only today -- CRITIQUE.md, PROJECT_OVERVIEW.md and SOLVE_SUMMARY.md, the last of which was publishing both totals on one page. NOT the figure the adjudication computed: it summed 2,759,921,108 by counting the four historical point-tests as a family and omitting the 10^5 random-Gray walks, 99,996 away from the roster SOLVE.md enumerates; that roster was used rather than re-derived. Allow column is documentation/HISTORY.md and only that file (it does not match PERFORMANCE_HISTORY.md): GUIDE.md records a 2026-08-30 decision that the dated aggregate in HISTORY.md is a correct record of the then-current roster and stays, so it is kept and annotated in place rather than overwritten, and every other file in the corpus is guarded.

column1: exactly the forward-reachable
column3: Retracted 2026-09-02 (Codex V2-F38 #1, prose batch P45): documentation/GT_LADDER_FORMAT.md's Stored-domains section described the g-ladder key restriction (last in the elements of the mask's pairs) as an exact characterization of the forward-reachable last values. The same document's "Expected boundary layers" section requires the seed layer n to store ALL 2n pair elements INCLUDING last values no valid prefix ever reaches, and its "What is convention vs derivable" section already called the restriction "pair-elements only" - so the spec contradicted itself, and the parenthetical was the wrong one of the three. The restriction is a SUPERSET relation and the stored set coincides with the forward-reachable set in neither direction: unreachable pair elements are stored at the seed with g = 1 by the empty-suffix convention, while a forward-reachable DEAD END has g = 0 and is skipped. Provenance of the wording: the section heading of roae-private/STAGE_G_FABLE_REVIEW_2026_07_17.md S1.3, whose body says the correct thing. NOT registered on the bare "forward-reachable", which is correct and load-bearing in reports/evidence/f1/FH1_RESIDUAL_DOMINANCE.md and lean/PruneExactness.lean. The identical sentence survives as a solve.c source comment on the v4-compiler branch at 453e1bf, outside GATE 3's markdown corpus and outside this batch's edit scope; it is queued for the code lane.

column1: are fully deterministic - output depends only on the King Wen sequence

The mechanism claim is the falsehood: those outputs are functions of RNG draws, not of the King Wen sequence alone. --complements happens to be byte-identical across seeds because its one-decimal summary concentrates -- empirical concentration at the current print precision, which one added decimal or a smaller trial count would break silently. Corrected form replaces the two-way split with the three-way one the code supports (12 seed-honouring, 1 internally pinned, 16 closed-form) and publishes an executable awk census. column1: L(C) plus the selection charge; prints survivors
column3: Retracted 2026-09-02 (Codex V2-F49 #5, prose batch P71): ROAE_PY_CLI.md described the U2 MDL ledger as comparing bits-explained against the statement cost plus the selection charge and then printing survivors, which reads as one bar. There are two. The detection-floor line applies the full bar; the survivor gate at roae.py:4382 is 'if be > L:' with no selection term, so a candidate between the two bars is printed as a SURVIVOR? line and flips the run verdict without having cleared the multiple-selection charge. ATTENTION fires from that same pre-selection list, and the JSON verdict and survivors fields carry no qualifier. The direction is over-flagging, not under-detection: nothing clearing the full bar is missed. Credited in the correction: the CODE already knows, labelling the tally MDL-net-positive (pre-selection) and ending each candidate line in a question mark; only the document did not say so. Corrected form tabulates the two bars. This batch owns the document, not roae.py, so the JSON pre-selection stamp is left to the code lane.
